{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Final check: revenue is string, but contains commas
print(f'Revenue dtype: {df["revenue"].dtype}')
print(f'Unique revenue values (first 10): {df["revenue"].unique()[:10]}')

# The issue is that '999,999.99' contains commas, so .astype(float) fails
# We must remove commas first
# Also verify QA count
qa_count = (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum()
print(f'QA rows count: {qa_count}')

# Now, strip commas and convert to float
df['revenue_float'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Now, filter for loyal customers and completed orders
loyal_completed = df[
    (df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & 
    (df['status'] == 'completed')
]

# Remove QA rows (revenue 999999.99)
loyal_completed_clean = loyal_completed[loyal_completed['revenue_float'] != 999999.99]

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = loyal_completed_clean['revenue_float'].mean()

# Output
mean_revenue"}
